questions.question: With no configuration, what runs in parallel?
options: Every test in the suite
Test files, while tests inside each file run in order
Nothing, until you set `workers`
Tests inside a file, while files run in order
questions.explanation: Files are spread across workers by default. Use `mode: 'parallel'` or `fullyParallel` to run the tests inside a file at the same time.

questions.question: Two tests in a file use `mode: 'parallel'` and write to a variable at the top of the file. What happens?
options: They share the variable, so writes can race
Playwright locks the variable between tests
The file fails to load
Each worker process has its own copy, so the value isn't shared
questions.explanation: Parallel tests run in separate worker processes, and each process loads the file for itself.

questions.question: A suite has one file with 50 tests and many small files. Why might `--shard=1/4` get far more work than `--shard=2/4` without `fullyParallel`?
options: A whole file goes to the shard where its first test lands
Shards are assigned by file size on disk
The first shard always runs the slowest tests
Shards share one queue at run time
questions.explanation: Shards balance test counts, but a file stays together unless `fullyParallel` lets its tests be placed one by one.

questions.question: What is the catch with `trace: 'on-first-retry'`?
options: It records every passing test
It only works in Chromium
It records nothing unless `retries` is above 0
It deletes the trace when the retry passes
questions.explanation: The trace is recorded during the first retry, so a config with no retries never produces one.

questions.question: Why start a `PerformanceObserver` for LCP with `page.addInitScript()`?
options: `page.evaluate()` can't use browser APIs
It makes the page load faster
It's the only way to read `window` values
The observer is in place before the page's own code runs
questions.explanation: An init script runs before the page's scripts, so the observer is ready from the start of the load.
